body.statement: Let \(C,C'\) be correlation matrices with \(\lambda_{\min}(C)\wedge\lambda_{\min}(C')\ge\eta\) and \(\lVert C-C'\rVert_{\max}\le\epsilon\). Under \(m\le d_{ej}\le M\), simultaneously for every order \(\pi\), \(\lVert B^{\pi}(C)-B^{\pi}(C')\rVert_{\max}\le2p^2\eta^{-2}\epsilon\) and \(\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\lVert\Phi_e^{\pi}(C;d)-\Phi_e^{\pi}(C';d)\rVert_{\max}\le14(M/m)p^4\eta^{-4}\epsilon\).
body.justification: This simultaneous modulus is the bridge from rank concentration to graph-valued inference over every candidate order.
body.gap: MitraZhang2014RankCorrelation, Theorem 2, controls rank-correlation submatrices, and Afsari2008JDSensitivity studies diagonalizer sensitivity; neither propagates errors uniformly through all projective Cholesky predictors.
body.consumer: Federated analysts obtain explicit penalties for weak correlation conditioning and dispersed normalized excitations.
